attribution: Traditionally attributed to Vyasa; composite authorship
author: vyasa
period: Scholars commonly place it between roughly the 9th and 14th centuries CE; dates are debated
summary: A large Shakta Purana presenting the Goddess as supreme reality, including the philosophical Devi Gita.
whyRead: It is the most extensive Puranic statement of Goddess-centred theology, joining myth and ritual with Vedantic philosophy. Its Devi Gita is a Goddess-centred counterpart to the Bhagavad Gita.
questions: How can the supreme be understood as feminine?
How does the Goddess relate to Brahman?

keyTeachings.title: The Goddess as Brahman
keyTeachings.text: The Devi is identified with Brahman, the ground of all, and the male gods act through her power.

keyTeachings.title: The Devi Gita
keyTeachings.text: In the seventh canto the Goddess teaches the mountain king Himalaya about the Self, yoga and devotion, drawing on Upanishadic and Vedantic ideas.

keyTeachings.title: Retold myths
keyTeachings.text: Many familiar stories are retold so that the Goddess is the decisive agent.

relatedTexts.note: The earlier core text of Goddess theology
Its structure and title parallel the Vaishnava Bhagavata
The Devi Gita is modelled in part on the Bhagavad Gita
